temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Thin, ¼ inch (6 mm) 375°F / 190°C · 12 min 400°F / 205°C · 17 min Standard, ⅜ inch (1 cm) 375°F / 190°C · 16 min 400°F / 205°C · 23 min Thick, ½ inch (1.3 cm) 375°F / 190°C · 20 min 400°F / 205°C · 29 min Dark edges, soft middles Sweet potatoes are not just orange potatoes. They contain far more sugar and much less of the starch that makes a white fry crisp. In the heat, that sugar caramelises and then burns at a lower temperature than starch browns, so the tips go dark and bitter while the rest is still soft. The soft part is the other half of the problem: with little starch to set into a rigid crust, a sweet potato fry tends to stay floppy however long it cooks. That is why this preset runs cooler than the white fry setting and for slightly less time, and why a light coat of cornstarch makes such a difference. The cornstarch supplies the dry starch layer the potato lacks, and it crisps in the air before the sugars underneath have time to scorch. Worked example Two medium sweet potatoes cut into ⅜-inch sticks, patted dry, tossed with a tablespoon of cornstarch, then a tablespoon of oil and a pinch of salt. Cook in one layer at 375°F for 16 minutes, shaking twice. Thin fries take about 12 minutes and thick ones about 20. Cook in batches; they crisp a little more as they cool for a minute. On a tray in a conventional oven: 400°F for around 23 minutes. How to tell they are done Look for edges that are browned and blistered but not black, and fries that hold their shape when lifted by one end rather than drooping. They will still be softer inside than a white fry; that is their nature. If the tips darken before the middles cook, cut the next batch a little thicker and more even rather than turning the heat up. Before they go in Peeling is optional; the skin crisps well. Cut sticks to an even thickness and skip the long soak used for white potatoes, since there is little surface starch to rinse off. Dry them, dust with cornstarch first and oil second, so the powder sticks. Season with smoked paprika or cinnamon, and salt again after cooking. About 16 minutes at 375°F for ⅜-inch fries, shaken twice. Thin fries take around 12 minutes and thick ones around 20. Why cook sweet potato fries cooler than regular fries? They contain much more sugar, which burns at a lower temperature than potato starch browns. A slightly cooler setting lets the inside cook before the edges blacken. How do I make sweet potato fries crispy? Dust them with cornstarch before the oil, cook in one layer and let them rest a minute after cooking. They never get quite as rigid as white fries. Do I need to soak sweet potato fries? No. The soak for white fries rinses off surface starch, and sweet potatoes have very little to remove. What is the oven equivalent for sweet potato fries? 400°F for around 23 minutes on a tray in a conventional oven, or 375°F for 18 minutes in a fan oven.
